title: Pupa
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Siblings Utsutsu and Yume, abandoned after years of abuse by their father, are caught up in a mysterious 'Pupa' condition: Yume becomes a flesh-eating monster, while Utsutsu gains regeneration and lets her feed on his body to keep her human. A cold researcher experiments on them, and later revelations recast the siblings' past, their parents and the origin of the monsters.
life_message: Unconditional love between siblings is shown holding on amid abuse and horror, though the story also questions whether such devotion is love or damage passed down.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Utsutsu answers threats to Yume personally and violently; no courts or rules in view (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Abandoned siblings live outside adult authority; institutions appear only as exploiters (Maria's lab).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Utsutsu's promise to protect Yume overrides all other lives (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Abusive parental authority is shown as harm, not deserving deference.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: A virus and lab research frame events, with island folklore underneath.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Daily survival, hunger and escape dominate the siblings' lives.

folkways.japan: Draws on the Momotaro-linked Onigashima ('ogre island') legend and on the shounen horror tradition of extreme body horror.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia and database summaries describe horror plot and twists, not stated lessons (to verify).

personified.ideology: Pain is the purest form of love, learned from Genjurou

delivery.note: The story offers horror and backstory rather than argument; the abusive and scientific worldviews are given origins but no rebuttal speeches.

winners_losers: The siblings' devotion survives at enormous cost; abusive adults and exploitative researchers drive the tragedy, and sympathy rests with the children.
